claims.text: Applying an aluminum oxide coating improves the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The intervention is the application of an aluminum oxide coating to an untreated refractory high-entropy alloy.
The coating forms a continuous aluminum oxide layer on the alloy surface.
The surface aluminum oxide layer remains stable under the stated high-temperature oxidation conditions.
The aluminum oxide layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into the alloy.
Restricting oxygen diffusion reduces oxidation reactions in the alloy.
The aluminum oxide coating will reduce the oxidation rate by at least 50% relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed improvement applies from 1000°C to 1200°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere for exposures of 100 to 500 hours.
An oxidation-rate result within 10% of the untreated-alloy rate after 200 hours at 1100°C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions field specifies temperatures above 1000°C, whereas the boundary explicitly includes 1000°C.
